'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Germany–Russia relations]], [[Germany–Poland relations]]
***[[Government of Germany|German]] [[Minister for Foreign Affairs (Germany)|Foreign Affairs Minister]] [[Annalena Baerbock]] says that [[Germany]] will not prevent [[Poland]] [[List of military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War|from sending]] [[Leopard 2]] [[main battle tank]]s to [[Ukraine]] which Ukrainian officials say are pivotal to defeating [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/france-does-not-rule-out-sending-leclerc-tanks-ukraine-macron-2023-01-22/ (Reuters)]
*[[Arab–Israeli conflict]]
**The [[Lebanese Armed Forces|Lebanese Army]] declares a "state of alert" after stopping [[Israel]]i [[bulldozer]]s and accompanying [[Israel Defense Forces|soldiers]] from approaching a border fence in [[Southern Lebanon]]. [[Peacekeeping]] forces from [[United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon|UNIFIL]] have also been deployed to the area. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/lebanon-army-declares-state-of-alert-amid-tension-with-israel/2794370# (AA)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Four people are killed and three others are feared dead in an apartment fire in [[Kobe]], [[Japan]]. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2023/01/22/national/kobe-apartment-fire/ (''The Japan Times'')]
*At least 13 people are killed when a five-story [[building collapse]]s in [[Aleppo]], [[Syria]], due to a leaking of water in the building's foundation. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/thirteen-killed-after-building-collapses-syrias-aleppo-state-media-2023-01-22/ (Reuters)]
*Four people are killed and six others are injured in a fire at a two-story [[cottage]] in [[Qusar (city)|Qusar]], [[Azerbaijan]]. [https://english.news.cn/20230122/089b3d191a7740d4ba14094cef312739/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Law enforcement in Cameroon|Police]] in [[Cameroon]] find the [[mutilation|mutilated]] body of prominent journalist [[Martinez Zogo]], who had been [[kidnap]]ped by unknown assailants five days ago, amid increasing violence against reporters in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/prominent-cameroon-journalist-found-dead-after-abduction-2023-01-22/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 New Zealand Labour Party leadership election]]
**The ruling [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour Party]] unanimously elects [[Minister of Education (New Zealand)|education]] and [[Public Service Commission (New Zealand)|public service minister]] [[Chris Hipkins]] to succeed [[Jacinda Ardern]] as [[Leader of the New Zealand Labour Party|the party's leader]] following Ardern's [[Resignation of Jacinda Ardern|resignation]] three days ago. [[Governor-General of New Zealand|Governor-General]] [[Cindy Kiro]] is expected to appoint Hipkins as the 41st [[prime minister of New Zealand]] on January 25. [https://apnews.com/article/politics-jacinda-ardern-new-zealand-f9cd3434bd1ac5a7d577963077a3ea4e (AP)]
*[[Israeli prime minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] dismisses [[Ministry of Health (Israel)|health]] and [[Ministry of Interior (Israel)|interior minister]] [[Aryeh Deri]] from [[Thirty-seventh government of Israel|his cabinet]] after the [[Supreme Court of Israel|Supreme Court]] ruled that Deri was barred from holding a position as a [[Cabinet of Israel|cabinet]] minister due to his conviction for [[Tax noncompliance|tax offenses]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230122-israel-pm-removes-top-minister-over-court-ruling (AFP via France 24)]

'''Sports'''
*In [[surfing]], American [[lifeguard]] Luke Shepardson wins the 2023 edition of [[The Eddie]] at [[Waimea Bay]] on the north shore of [[Oahu]], [[Hawaii]], United States, after finishing with 89.1 points out of 90, defeating defending champion [[John John Florence]]. [https://apnews.com/article/sports-john-florence-hawaii-surfing-57725912ad9128d34cc09558a33311e5 (AP)]
